findings.affected_surface: HTTP Content-Length header validation in soup_message_headers_append_common
findings.old_behavior: Content-Length header values that overflow uint64 in g_ascii_strtoull were accepted. Two distinct overflowing values would both saturate to G_MAXUINT64 and incorrectly pass the equality check, allowing the duplicate Content-Length header to be appended.
findings.new_behavior: Prior to each g_ascii_strtoull call, errno is cleared to 0. After parsing, if the value overflowed (errno == ERANGE), the function returns FALSE, rejecting the Content-Length header as invalid. Overflows are now properly detected and rejected.
findings.compatibility_reason: The patch tightens the input validation contract for Content-Length header parsing. Previously, overflowed values that saturated to G_MAXUINT64 were silently accepted by the library. After the patch, these same values are rejected with FALSE. Any libsoup-based HTTP client or server that relied on the old behavior (e.g., proxied traffic with malformed Content-Length headers) may experience connection failures or request rejections after update. While this is a correctness fix per RFC 9110 §8.6, it narrows the set of accepted inputs and is externally observable as changed HTTP header processing behavior.
findings.why_not_internal_only: The function soup_message_headers_append_common is the dispatch target for soup_message_headers_append (public API, declared in soup-message-headers.h). It processes untrusted HTTP Content-Length header values from incoming network requests. Changes directly affect HTTP protocol compliance and behavior visible to remote peers and API consumers.
findings.uncertainty: Low uncertainty. The before/after contract is precisely defined by the diff hunk. The change is a straightforward errno-based overflow guard with no edge cases that would circumvent the check.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that no downstream consumers depend on overflowed Content-Length values being silently accepted. The fix aligns with RFC 9110 §8.6 (Content-Length field value must be a valid decimal) and is a correctness improvement, but any intermediary that forwards malformed headers could break.
findings.test_recommendation: Test with valid Content-Length values (within uint64 range), boundary values (0, 1, G_MAXUINT64), and overflow values (G_MAXUINT64+1, large numbers exceeding 2^64-1). Verify proper return value (FALSE for invalid/overflow) and that valid duplicate Content-Length headers still pass. Test whitespace variants and negative values as already covered by header-parsing-test.
